human_views.edit_policy: Change canonical data first; then update or regenerate the human view in the same commit.

primary.lexical_meaning: YHWH is salvation / the LORD saves

scriptural_descriptors.descriptor: servant of the LORD at death

leadership.calling: Lead Israel across the Jordan, apportion the land, act courageously, and keep the law.

failures_and_limits.summary: Israel's leaders did not ask counsel from the LORD before the Gibeonite treaty; Joshua made peace and a covenant with them.
Defeat at Ai demonstrates that Joshua's command did not make victory automatic amid covenant violation.
The narrative states that very much land remained to be possessed.
Hebrews distinguishes Joshua's rest from the further rest proclaimed afterward.

lifespan.chronology_note: Absolute dates are intentionally unresolved because the project does not adjudicate disputed chronologies.

summary.defining_contribution: Led Israel across the Jordan and through the land-entry campaigns, apportioned inheritance, and renewed covenant at Shechem.
summary.canonical_summary: Joshua son of Nun, an Ephraimite and Moses' commissioned successor, leads with courage grounded in the LORD's presence and obedience to the law.

classification_policy.scripture: Claim explicitly stated or directly reported in the cited passage.
classification_policy.traditional_understanding: Received interpretive or lexical understanding, not an explicit narrative gloss.
classification_policy.responsible_synthesis: Project synthesis constrained by multiple cited passages.
classification_policy.project_interpretation: Creative product decision that must not be presented as Scripture.

events.title: Leads battle against Amalek
events.summary: Joshua commands Israel's fighters while the narrative locates victory beyond military action alone.

events.title: Assists Moses at Sinai
events.summary: Joshua accompanies Moses and descends with him.

events.title: Remains near the tent
events.summary: Joshua's assistant role continues near the tent without assuming Moses' unique role.

events.title: Responds to Eldad and Medad
events.summary: Joshua's loyalty to Moses becomes an occasion for instruction about prophetic participation.

events.title: Scouts Canaan and stands with Caleb
events.summary: Joshua and Caleb urge trust in the LORD against the majority report.

events.title: Commissioned before Eleazar and Israel
events.summary: Responsibility is publicly transferred under divine direction.

events.title: Charged by Moses and the LORD
events.summary: Courage is grounded in divine presence and the assigned commission.

events.title: Assumes leadership after Moses' death
events.summary: Joshua begins the land-entry commission as Moses' successor.

events.title: Sends spies and receives Rahab's aid
events.summary: The spies' oath establishes the promise later honored toward Rahab's household.

events.title: Leads the Jordan crossing and memorial
events.summary: Israel crosses on dry ground and establishes twelve memorial stones for future teaching.

events.title: Renews covenant signs and observes Passover
events.summary: Entry is framed by covenant practice and Passover.

events.title: Encounters the commander of the LORD's army
events.summary: Joshua is placed beneath rather than identified with the mysterious commander.

events.title: Jericho falls and Rahab is spared
events.summary: Ordered obedience precedes the wall's fall and Joshua honors the oath concerning Rahab.

events.title: Faces Achan's violation and returns to Ai
events.summary: Defeat, exposed violation, judgment, and renewed action show that victory is not automatic.

events.title: Builds altar and reads the law at Ebal
events.summary: Covenant instruction remains central to Joshua's leadership.

events.title: Makes the Gibeonite treaty and leads the southern campaign
events.summary: The account includes failed counsel, oath obligation, defense, and military deliverance.

events.title: Leads northern campaign
events.summary: Campaign summaries consolidate land-entry leadership while later text still notes remaining land.

events.title: Oversees allotments and receives Timnath-serah
events.summary: Joshua stewards tribal inheritance and receives his own inheritance after the tribes.

events.title: Resolves the eastern-tribes altar dispute
events.summary: Inquiry and explanation prevent covenant misunderstanding from becoming conflict.

events.title: Gives farewell and renews covenant at Shechem
events.summary: Joshua calls Israel to exclusive service of the LORD and records covenant witness.

events.title: Dies and is buried at Timnath-serah
events.summary: Joshua dies at 110; the narrative records continued influence through the elders who outlive him.

relationships.influence: Source of Joshua's authority, presence, covenant accountability, and victory.
Moses prepares, commissions, and publicly confirms Joshua without erasing Moses' unique prophetic standing.
They share a faithful minority report; Caleb retains a distinct inheritance story.
Joshua's leadership is publicly accountable and works with priestly office.
Connects Jericho with oath-keeping and rescue; no personal pre-rescue meeting is stated.
Priests carry the ark and trumpets in ordered covenant action rather than serving as decorative soldiers.
Joshua's leadership is corporate and covenantal.
Elders share public responsibility and continue influence after Joshua's death.
The Ai crisis demonstrates covenant accountability and the limits of command.
Records failed counsel, oath obligation, and subsequent defense.
Shows shared service, misunderstanding, investigation, and restored peace.
Reorients Joshua beneath divine command; the figure's further identity remains unresolved.
Supplies campaign context without authorizing racial caricature or spectacle of suffering.

prohibited_visual_concepts.reason: Joshua must not control divine power.
The commander of the LORD's army must not be merged with Joshua.

gameplay.theme: Ordered allied participation creates an opening against fortifications and converts secured ground into inheritance.
gameplay.player_promise: My army advances together, barriers open, and claimed ground becomes inheritance.

preferred_mechanics.concept: Reward multiple allied roles acting in sequence.
Resist fear or morale disruption under covenant conditions.
Answer defenses after coordinated preparation rather than personal magic.
Open a route through terrain or control effects using event or support framing.
Place persistent advantage after securing and holding an objective.
Leadership loses efficiency when formation acts presumptuously or breaks faith.

differentiation.distinction: Moses liberates and controls barriers; Joshua advances
Caleb is an enduring individual claimant; Joshua is a whole-army commander.

signature_ability.name: Walls Fall Down
signature_ability.concept: Break a fortification only after coordinated allied participation, then convert the opened objective into persistent positional advantage.

art.classification_note: Physical appearance is project interpretation; Scripture does not describe Joshua's face, hair, beard, build, or campaign age.

open_findings.summary: Confirm the Ark and divine agency boundaries before generation.
Confirm whether visible bronze torso armour should remain optional.
